Department All Employee Category All Clear Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Create Alert × Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Apply now » Research Assistant Job Req ID: 2597 Employee Category: Research Department: DmanD Centre Research Officer in Textile Fabrication and Characterisation for Wearable Energy Harvesting We are seeking a motivated Research Officer with interest in textile fabrication, and materials characterisation to join our interdisciplinary team developing next-generation knitted wearable systems for sensing and energy harvesting. The successful candidate will play a central role in the design, fabrication, and testing of knitted structures using a CNC knitting machine, with a particular focus on engineering textile architectures for energy harvesting applications. You will work closely with researchers in electronics, CNC knitting, and modelling to translate material and structural concepts into functional knitted prototypes for body-worn systems. Key Responsibilities You will be expected to: Design and fabricate knitted structures using a CNC knitting machine for wearable sensing and energy harvesting applications. Develop and optimise knit architectures, yarn selections, stitch patterns, and structural parameters to improve mechanical performance and energy harvesting capability. Characterise knitted fabrics under controlled laboratory and body-worn conditions, including mechanical, structural, and functional testing. Support the development of textile samples for triboelectric, piezoelectric, and related wearable transducer systems. Investigate the influence of knitting parameters on fabric properties such as stretch, durability, porosity, comfort, and transduction performance. Collaborate with electronic engineers to ensure knitted structures are compatible with sensor integration, signal acquisition, and power harvesting systems. Work with computational modellers to relate textile design variables to experimental performance. Contribute to research outputs, including journal publications, conference presentations, and stakeholder enagements. Requirements Bachelor’s degree or higher in Materials Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Textile Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Practical experience in fabrication, prototyping, and experimental characterisation of engineered materials or structures. Hands-on experience with textile manufacturing, knit design, or CNC knitting processes is desirable. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work across disciplinary boundaries. Experience using laboratory instrumentation and/or mechanical testing methods for material or textile characterisation. Department All Employee Category All Clear Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Create Alert × Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Apply now » Research Fellow I Job Req ID: 2584 Employee Category: Research Department: EPD Pillar Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Silicon Photonics and Advanced Photonic Packaging The Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to work on advanced photonic packaging and silicon photonics. The project focuses on developing low-loss optical coupling and packaging solutions for photonic integrated circuits, including chip-to-fibre, chip-to-chip, and chip-to-free-space interfaces. We are seeking candidates with strong experience in silicon photonics, waveguide optics, and photonic device design. Hands-on experience in building optical test setups and characterizing integrated photonic devices is highly desirable. Responsibilities Lead the design and simulation of silicon photonic devices, waveguides, mode converters, optical couplers, and packaging interfaces using commercial photonic design tools. Perform optical simulations and tolerance analyses to optimize coupling efficiency, bandwidth, alignment tolerance, and packaging performance. Build and operate optical characterization setups using tunable lasers, optical spectrum analyzers, power meters, cameras, fibre alignment stages, and related equipment. Characterize fabricated devices and packaged photonic systems, including insertion loss, spectral response, polarization dependence, and alignment tolerance. Work with interdisciplinary academic and industrial partners on device fabrication, packaging, system integration, and end-to-end validation. Contribute to research publications, technical reports, patent applications, and project proposals. Qualifications Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Photonics, Optical Engineering, or a closely related field. Strong background in silicon photonics, integrated photonics, waveguide optics, or photonic integrated circuits. Demonstrated experience in photonic device design, numerical simulation, and layout. Proficiency with relevant design and simulation tools, such as Ansys Lumerical, COMSOL, MATLAB, or Python. Hands-on experience in constructing optical test setups and characterizing integrated photonic devices. Familiarity with optical components and equipment such as tunable lasers, optical spectrum analyzers, power meters, polarization controllers, probe stations, and fibre alignment stages. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary research environment. Preferred Experience Experience with experimental tests of photonic integrated circuits. Experience in waveguide, grating coupler, edge coupler, mode converter, or freeform optical component design. Experience with active alignment, automated optical testing, or packaging-tolerance analysis. Knowledge of optical communication systems, co-packaged optics, or high-speed photonic systems. Familiarity with micro- and nanofabrication processes is an advantage. Appointment and Salary The position will be based at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), Singapore. The initial appointment is expected to be for one year, with the possibility of renewal subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability. Successful candidates will join an active group of Principal Investigators and researchers to work within the Aviation Studies Institute (ASI) of SUTD. ASI was established jointly with the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) in 2019. Our goal is to establish a world-leading centre of aviation policy research and thought leadership. We are dedicated to address the needs of aviation stakeholders in general and Air Traffic Management (ATM) policy makers in particular to advance the development of aviation in the Asia-Pacific region. The candidates will be advancing the state of airport operations and envisaging the airport of the future while making excellent scholarly contributions and innovations for transition to practice. Topics include, but are not limited to, robotics and automation in aircraft turnaround, digital apron connectivity, optimization of ground service equipment, process mapping and stakeholder management. An ideal candidate will have a PhD with expertise in one (or) more of the following areas: Robotics and Automation, especially with contact-rich tasks; Operations Research, with expertise in optimisation; Computer Science, with expertise in design and analysis of algorithms and high-performance (GPU) computing; Industrial and Systems Engineering, with AI in process mapping and Conops design. With SUTD located next to the number #1-ranked airport in the world (Singapore’s Changi Airport) and a stimulating aviation ecosystem, there will be plenty of opportunities to work closely with industry experts to tackle the challenges in airport modernisation and operations excellence.
